The Puzzlers' Pigeonhole

CountingParityCoordinates
Game: Dots stand on the corners of a grid. Look for two dots with a corner exactly halfway between them.
How to play: Drag a dot to another corner, or use the arrow keys on a selected dot. Can you move four dots so that no two have a corner halfway between? Can you do it with five?
Look for the math

If you choose five corners of a square grid, some two of them always have a corner exactly halfway between them. With four it can be avoided. That is the pigeonhole principle at work: if more objects than boxes are put in boxes, some box gets two.

When is the middle a corner?

The midpoint of (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is ((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2). It is a corner exactly when x1+x2 and y1+y2 are both even: that is, when the two x's are both odd or both even, and the same for the y's.

Four boxes

Each corner has one of four parities: odd/odd, odd/even, even/odd or even/even. These are the four boxes. Five dots must put two in the same box, and two dots in one box have a corner halfway between them. The test confirmed it for every set of five corners of a 4×4 patch and for 200,000 random positions on this board. With four dots the only way to avoid a pair is one dot in each box: the test found exactly 94 = 6561 such sets of four on a 6×6 patch, and none other. Also, such a segment passes through other corners besides the midpoint when the differences share a common factor.

Place four dots with no halfway corner, then add a fifth: where can you put it so that there is only one pair?

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
